name: rt_stairwell_concept
subject: the tall grey block on the right is the front of an ochre plaster house with rows of windows (stairwell house A); the grey slope rising to the right along its front is a long flight of stone steps built against the house, each step a flat stone tread, with an iron handrail on posts; the flat ground on the left is the cobbled street with its granite pavement; the grey blocks behind on the left are old town houses with windows and red tile roofs

slot.where: Rooftops, the stairwell steps up from the street, camera y 960 x 400

extra: Image 2 is the approved painting of the hotel roof in this same level: use exactly its materials, colours, light, dark outlines and pixel size (warm ochre plaster walls, sandstone parapet caps in blocks, red clay roof tiles, green copper, stucco chimney stacks with clay pots, glass lanterns in black iron frames, dark brown window frames); do not copy its buildings or its layout. Replace every grey placeholder shape completely with finished art, nothing see-through, no grey left. Surfaces as flat shapes with 1 px joints, not texture. Behind the near roofs, the far town as its own clean band of red roofs, chimneys and the church spire, lighter and softer in colour than the near roofs; the roofs and edges the dog walks on are the darkest and most contrasted. No stone rows that look like ledges just above the dog's head. Every drop reads as an opening. Keep the dog exactly as it is; keep the small grey metal vent boxes and the orange loose tiles where they are. This painting will be reduced back to the game's 320x240 grid and cut into separate game pieces, so keep the quality of Image 2 exactly: draw on the pixel grid of Image 1, every pixel square and the size of the dog's pixels, aligned to the same grid; one flat colour per pixel, no in-between edge colours, no smudges or painterly strokes; every building part, chimney, window, railing and prop drawn whole, with crisp dark outlines and clear separate shapes as in Image 2, so each can be cut out on its own; the same crispness and level of detail as Image 2.
